blurb: Family of agile, intelligent herding dogs from Scotland and Northern England
description: The Collie is a type of medium-sized herding dog from Scotland and Northern England, lightly built with a pointed snout, agile, intelligent and gentle.
answer: Collies are a distinctive type of herding dog that originated in Scotland and Northern England, covering many landraces and formal breeds such as the Rough, Smooth and Border Collie. They are medium-sized, fairly lightly built dogs with pointed snouts. Collies are known as active, agile and intelligent, with a strong herding instinct.

body: Herding dogs of collie type have long been widespread in Britain and form a landrace from which many types and breeds were derived, including the Border Collie, Rough and Smooth Collies, Bearded Collie and Shetland Sheepdog, as well as the Australian Kelpie and other overseas breeds. The origin of the name is uncertain; it may come from the Scots word for coal or from a word for Scotland's black-faced sheep. In parts of the US the plain name Collie usually means the Rough Collie, while in rural Britain it often means the Border Collie.

Collies are medium-sized and light to medium-boned, with cattle-herding types stockier than sheep-herding types. The coat may be short or long, and the tail smooth, feathered or bushy, never carried over the back. Common colors include sable, black and white, black and tan, tricolor and merle, often with white on the chest, belly, shoulders and face, sometimes forming a mane.

Collie breeds are generally described as highly trainable, gentle, loyal and intelligent, and often good with children. They are known for sensitivity to people's emotions and may need gentler handling than other dogs. Working strains such as the Border Collie are energetic, highly motivated and can be single-minded; dogs of collie type hold four of the first sixteen places in Stanley Coren's intelligence ranking.

All collie types need some mental stimulation, and the Border Collie in particular needs a job or it may become anxious and hyperactive. Collies excel at herding, sheepdog trials, flyball, disc dog and agility, and Border Collies serve as mountain rescue search dogs in Britain.

Conditions reported in collies include the MDR1 mutation, which lowers tolerance to many veterinary drugs and is reported in about 70 percent of collies, as well as canine cyclic neutropenia (grey collie syndrome), familial dermatomyositis and Collie eye anomaly. MDR1 status can be tested, and the German Kennel Club encourages testing of breeding stock.

faq.q: Is the Collie a single breed?
faq.a: Collie describes a type of herding dog that includes many breeds and landraces. The American Kennel Club has a breed it calls the Collie, the name usually means the Rough Collie in parts of the US, and it often means the Border Collie in rural Britain.
Collie breeds are generally described as gentle, devoted and compatible with children, though individual personalities vary.
Collies range from average to very biddable in trainability, and the Border Collie ranks first in Stanley Coren's intelligence list.
MDR1 is a genetic mutation that makes affected dogs unusually sensitive to many drugs, including ivermectin. A simple test can identify a dog's status.
